excluded_from_promotion.csql.err: CUBRID client-side connect log. Inspected before exclusion: it contains only 'Program csql ... connected' NOTIFICATION lines and boot_cl.c:875 CODE=-971 notifications, i.e. one entry per client connection this session opened. No error, no failed statement.
excluded_from_promotion.perf-*.data: raw perf sample files (0.9-2.3 GB each, 4.6 GB total). The derived profile-*-flat.txt / profile-*-callgraph.txt reports and the perf-stat-*.txt counters are promoted and hashed, and every profile number in the report is read from those. The .data files themselves are dispensable work and were DELETED at query completion together with the rest of work/Q21 (SSOT section 19: 'promote required files to raw and delete dispensable work'). They are reproducible from raw/Q21/hltel_profile_driver.sh against the pinned binaries.

notes: Q21 needed NO re-measurement and NO server restart. cub_server pid 2646189 and postmaster pid 1433696 are the same processes, at the same executable SHA-256, before the first block and after the last (q21-preflight.txt / q21-postflight.txt), with 30 engine TIDs and 0 off-cpuset on both gates and ssot_drift=NONE on both.

NEITHER ENGINE IS RESIDENT ON Q21, BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS NOT A WARM FAILURE. The referenced relations are lineitem (10,671 MiB heap, 682,937 CUBRID pages) and orders (2,370 MiB, 151,689 pages) against the contracted 8192 MB pool on both sides. The section 12 requirement met here is the one that applies: the LEVEL is proved steady by a per-configuration convergence probe and the physical-read deltas are RECORDED -- CUBRID 670,565 page reads (10.23 GiB) per statement native and 1,018,456 (15.54 GiB) controlled, PostgreSQL 349,789 (2.24 GiB), all from /proc syscr+rchar on the block telemetry. DEVICE reads are zero on every configuration (/proc read_bytes delta 0), so every miss is served by the OS page cache.

cubrid statdump buffer counters again read delta 0 over a whole block on this server (Q14/Q16/Q18/Q19/Q20 defect, reconfirmed here on a 200 s block where even Num_data_page_fetches read 0 while the engine trace reports 1,016,255 page fetches for a single statement). The gauges are retained inside the headline JSONs but are EXCLUDED from every calculation; CUBRID buffer/IO evidence rests on /proc read_bytes+syscr+rchar and on the engine trace instead.

F_plan ANCHOR. Q21 is a query CUBRID loses and the plan defect is CUBRID's, so the anchor is CUBRID native -> CUBRID controlled (q21-late.sql). The controlled variant writes the same four-way join as a derived table so the two correlated sublinks reference the derived spec instead of lineitem l1; the only other token added is a LIMIT 2147483647 inside the derived table, whose sole function is to stop CUBRID's view merging from flattening the derived spec back into the original plan. That the plain derived-table form IS flattened is itself recorded evidence (q21-plan-est-late.out: byte-identical plan and cost 123,427,506 to the native q21-plan-est-cubrid.out). The controlled variant returns the byte-identical 100-row result on the same engine, verified row by row against the native block sink (q21-late-result-cubrid.out vs sink/Q21-cubrid-headline-block1.out).

WARM-GATE COST, recorded because it is large and because every rejection is kept. Nine 12-statement CUBRID warm-up runs were rejected across the six CUBRID blocks (native block2 attempt 1, block3 attempts 1-3; controlled block1 attempts 1-2, block3 attempts 1-4). All accepted blocks passed the INHERITED gate; nothing was relaxed. A moving-block bootstrap over all 76 CUBRID steady-state statements (q21-warm-gate-bootstrap.txt) shows the inherited LEVEL_TOL of 1.0% sits near the null p75 for this query (n=12 null p95 1.8278%, max 3.2699%), so the rejections are false negatives; the derived-but-unapplied gate is recorded in q21-warm-gate-params.txt for the next ~50 s query.

TWO NON-HEADLINE WARM RUNS DID NOT CONVERGE and are declared rather than hidden: the CUBRID controlled trace warm-up and the PostgreSQL EXPLAIN warm-up in plan_act_driver.sh both returned rc=4 (q21-cubrid-late-trace-warm.log, q21-pg-explain-warm.log; the PostgreSQL one reports steady 3.053904 s against the block level of 3.083188 s, i.e. 0.95% low). Neither feeds a headline or a card input: the artifacts they precede are the trace and the EXPLAIN (ANALYZE), which are read for COUNTS and plan shape, not for time. Every count they produce is independently confirmed by the COUNT(*) ground-truth probe.

Q21's traced statement costs 65.40 s against the 49.39 s headline (+32.4%): SET TRACE ON is itself instrumentation on a plan that performs 35,975,762 correlated subquery evaluations. No trace TIME is used anywhere in the report or the card; only readkeys/rows/fetch/ioread COUNTS are, and those are cross-checked against the independent ground truth.
